exact_r3_scope.title: Restore fresh-plan A→B→A stale-identity reactivation

accepted_invariant.fresh_planning: A later eligible fresh planner decision may choose stale stable identity A again after A→B, give that new planning occurrence a newer authoritative ordering position, and make A current/claimable again.
accepted_invariant.old_queue_delivery: A stale/cancelled task remains terminal for old Queue delivery/retry; Queue delivery alone must not reactivate it.
accepted_invariant.completed_identity: A completed stable identity remains terminal and must not be reopened by duplicate Queue delivery or duplicate/fresh planning of the same completed identity.
accepted_invariant.stable_identity: Stable task identity/id semantics are preserved; sourceFingerprint/taskIdentity/generationPolicyVersion are semantic identity inputs, not chronological ordering values.
accepted_invariant.ordering: Monotonic generation ordering and the generation-head serialization point remain authoritative.
accepted_invariant.fencing: Claim-token and current-generation publication fencing remain authoritative; superseded work cannot publish current state.

defect_currentness.proof: Current upsertPending returns an existing stale identity unchanged whenever existing.generation !== currentGeneration. After A(gen1)→B(gen2), stale A cannot become current on a later fresh A plan.
The accepted PR #72 review finding (discussion_r4028280128) exactly matches the current store branch; post-R2 main retains the PR #72 task-store blob.
The non-current stale early return is still present verbatim in current db/translation-task-store.ts.
PersistentTranslationJobDispatcher still enqueues the task returned by upsertPending; therefore the unchanged stale A is enqueued when fresh planning returns it.
claim() still only transitions pending or expired processing rows; on stale/completed it returns terminal, so the re-enqueued unchanged stale A cannot execute.
PR #83 restored the broad fresh-plan A→B→A contract in PROVIDERS_AND_JOBS.md, while current store behavior remains current-only stale reactivation. The code/contract mismatch therefore still exists.

PR #83 corrected the historical current-only documentation wording, so R3 must not edit that document again. The atomic record remains part of the accepted CD-11/REM-05 accounting because the implementation still has the exact current-only behavior the documentation correction was meant to reject.

checks: Checked whether PR #86 modified the task store, dispatcher, consumer, task generation tests, or publication store: it did not.
Checked whether stable task identity changes on semantic revert A→B→A: it does not; uiTranslationJobIdentity is deterministic over semantic inputs, so A is recreated as the same stable identity.
Checked whether current upsertPending can reactivate stale A after B becomes current: it cannot because the stale reactivation branch requires existing.generation === currentGeneration.
Checked whether Queue delivery can independently revive stale A: it cannot; claim returns terminal for stale/completed, which is accepted and must be preserved.
Checked whether completed A can reopen: current store/publication tests keep completed identity terminal; R3 must preserve this.

Checked whether existing durable fields can express a fresh A occurrence safely: generation is not immutable in schema, generation-head row already serializes planning/publication, and the accepted plan explicitly lists reuse of the stale stable row with a new generation as viable.

Checked whether a new schema object is required to distinguish the fresh planning decision: not required by the accepted invariant if the existing stale row is atomically moved to a newer generation under the locked head.
Checked whether current docs still need the PR #72 current-only wording correction: no; PR #83 already restored the accepted broad A→B→A contract.
strongest_counterevidence: Current single-identity stale reactivation already works when stale A is still current; this proves the defect is specifically cross-identity A→B→A rather than all stale reactivation.
Existing concurrent-planning tests prove head-row serialization and monotonic ordering work for different identities.
Existing publication tests prove generation/claim fencing and completed terminality are already working foundations and should not be redesigned.
deliberate_disconfirmation.result: The defect remains current, but the existing schema/fencing foundation is sufficient for a bounded store-level correction.

reason: The accepted plan prefers no schema expansion when existing durable fields can prove the invariant.

Current translation_tasks already stores stable identity, lifecycle state, and mutable generation; translation_task_generation_heads already provides the serialized monotonic current-generation authority.
A stale stable row can receive a newer generation/current position atomically under the existing head lock without changing task identity, claim/publication contracts, or schema.
No accepted invariant requires retaining a separate historical row for each planning occurrence.
schema_and_migration.boundary: If implementation proves the existing schema cannot satisfy race-safety or terminality, do not add a migration under this preflight; stop and revise the preflight first.

required_behavior: Fresh A after A→B may reactivate only when A is stale and the action is a fresh planner/store upsert.
Reactivation must assign A a newer authoritative generation than B and atomically advance the generation head under the existing serialization lock.
Reactivation clears stale/old-claim lifecycle metadata consistently with pending state.
Duplicate planning of already pending/processing current A must not reset or extend a live claim.
Completed A remains unchanged and terminal.
Old stale Queue delivery before fresh planner action remains terminal.
Superseded generation and lost-claim publication fencing remains unchanged.
